SMTO-GWT-0021 — The Gateway refused a request because the clocks don't match

GUID: 7942ffd3-7b8f-412a-941e-bdef95a10203
Slug: request-timestamp-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Every request SMTO sends to the Gateway is stamped with the time. The Gateway's clock and the SMTO server's clock disagree by more than a minute, so the request was refused and nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the computer running the Gateway, open its date and time settings and turn on setting the time automatically. Check that the time zone is correct too. The Gateway refuses any request whose time stamp is more than a minute away from its own clock.
  2. Do the same on the computer that runs the SMTO server. SMTO stamps each request with the server's time, so both clocks must agree.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. This sends a new, freshly stamped request and shows whether the Gateway now accepts it.
  4. Send your request again from the conversation. The refused request never ran, so repeating it does not do the work twice.

What success looks like

  • Check connection reports the Gateway as connected, and your request runs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO and the Gateway computer. Don't keep resending the same request until the clocks are fixed; it will be refused every time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway request authentication rejected the signed request because its timestamp was malformed or more than 60 seconds away from the verifier's clock.

What this means

  • Request freshness validation rejected a malformed timestamp or one more than sixty seconds from the verifier's clock. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Request freshness validation rejected a malformed timestamp or one more than sixty seconds from the verifier's clock.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare both host clocks and the retained request timestamp format; distinguish clock skew from a delayed or reused request.

How to fix it

  • Compare the system clocks on the Server host and the Gateway host and enable NTP time sync on both (for example timedatectl set-ntp true on Linux, or Windows automatic time). The window is 60 seconds (gateway_core.client_auth.fresh); after the clocks agree, issue a new request so a fresh timestamp and nonce are signed.
  • Synchronize clocks on the controller and Gateway hosts, then generate a fresh authenticated request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Correctly synchronized hosts accept a newly signed request within the freshness window.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.
